rationales.quote: four million, it's a lot of money
rationales.explanation: Jenny flags the requested raise as unusually large and asks how it will be allocated and what milestones it should achieve.

rationales.quote: I think that's just healthcare. That's not you.
rationales.explanation: Jenny argues that the slow sales cycle reflects healthcare purchasing rather than founder-specific execution weakness.

rationales.quote: This is not going to change.
rationales.explanation: Jenny emphasizes that the healthcare sales-cycle constraint is persistent.

rationales.quote: you're incredibly impressive
rationales.explanation: Jenny expresses a strongly favorable view of the founder personally.

rationales.quote: you have just like hustled, you know, the hell out of this business
rationales.explanation: Jenny credits the founder's resourcefulness and effort in advancing the company.

rationales.quote: with multiple business models
rationales.explanation: Jenny views the simultaneous business-model paths as difficult to evaluate and part of why she declines.

rationales.quote: a $4 million raise, which is, you know, quite high for me as a pre-seed
rationales.explanation: Jenny says the round size is large relative to her pre-seed investing constraints.

rationales.quote: I have a business here
rationales.explanation: Jenny believes the company already has a viable business before the later FDA expansion.

rationales.quote: she reversed the order and that confused us
rationales.explanation: Jenny says the presentation sequence obscured the otherwise attractive business path.

rationales.quote: Too many things.
rationales.explanation: Jenny characterizes the simultaneous initiatives as excessive complexity in the plan.

rationales.quote: she is in a great position
rationales.explanation: Despite the plan complexity, Jenny believes the company has a strong underlying position.

rationales.quote: she didn't have all our numbers
rationales.explanation: Jenny agrees that the financial case was not fully supported by the numbers presented.

rationales.quote: This is pretty cool.
rationales.explanation: Jenny expresses a favorable reaction to the product.

rationales.quote: she kind of didn't give me a convincing answer
rationales.explanation: Jenny says the founder failed to convincingly explain the rationale for the proposed approach.

rationales.quote: this is the best way to accumulate the data
rationales.explanation: Jenny rejects the stated data-accumulation strategy as insufficiently credible.

rationales.quote: that's health care, and that's not bad
rationales.explanation: Jenny treats six-month healthcare sales cycles as normal rather than a negative market signal.

rationales.quote: it can take a very long time
rationales.explanation: Jenny reiterates that lengthy healthcare purchasing cycles are an expected market condition.

rationales.quote: toughen up there lady
rationales.explanation: Jenny criticizes the founder's resilience in responding to normal healthcare sales-cycle friction.

rationales.quote: do they feel like they're being tracked in some way that makes them uncomfortable?
rationales.explanation: Jenny asks whether perceived tracking creates user resistance that could affect adoption.

question is queried/neutral, not a negative belief. Greetings, jokes, biography, simple confirmations and bare In/Out without
a reason are not rationales. Distinguish closely related taxonomy definitions; do not add broad redundant labels.
Retain each distinct rationale-bearing target utterance and exact evidence turn. Multiple labels on a turn are allowed only
when distinct concepts are expressed. For a repeated concept in different substantive turns retain each occurrence.
Quotes must be exact nonempty substrings of that turn's attributed_text, never continuation narration or another speaker.
The full text is included for context, but only attributed_text is eligible quote evidence.
Classify timing: original_pitch includes Q&A AND the entire original in-room decision discussion; later_commentary includes
post-pitch interviews, later diligence and subsequent updates; teaser is an opening preview/repeated future clip. Use unclear
when timing is uncertain. Do not use the redacted input cutoff as the end of original in-room discussion. Same-session
reversals stay original_pitch. Immediate investor-only debrief in the same room after the founder exits also stays
original_pitch; it is NOT later_commentary. Reserve later_commentary for separate interviews, diligence or updates. Do not mix retrospective opinions into original-pitch scoring.
Direction is positive/negative/neutral towards investing in this company. Salience primary means a stated major reason, not
merely any question. decision_link supports_in/out ONLY if the target links the rationale to the commitment/refusal.
Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.

rationales.quote: So does that mean the FDA is like a 510 or it's a, it's one of these lesser -
rationales.explanation: Jenny asks which FDA pathway the product must navigate, probing the operational burden of approval.

rationales.quote: So that's going to be shorter and less expensive.
rationales.explanation: Before being corrected, Jenny assesses the stated pathway as favorable because she believes it will require less time and capital.

rationales.quote: four million, it's a lot of money
rationales.explanation: Jenny flags the requested capital as substantial before asking how it will be deployed.

rationales.quote: what the metrics you hope to get to?
rationales.explanation: Jenny asks what measurable progress the proposed financing is expected to produce.

rationales.quote: And how's the fundraise going?
rationales.explanation: Jenny asks about current investor demand for the round.

rationales.quote: Are you looking for a lead investor? Or how are you putting the round together?
rationales.explanation: Jenny probes whether the round has or needs a lead and how its commitments are being assembled.

rationales.quote: I think that's just healthcare. That's not you.
rationales.explanation: Jenny argues that the slow sales cycle is normal for healthcare rather than evidence of founder-specific execution weakness.

rationales.quote: This is not going to change.
rationales.explanation: Jenny emphasizes that long healthcare sales cycles will remain a persistent constraint on the sales motion.

rationales.quote: I love your background
rationales.explanation: Jenny favorably assesses the founder's relevant professional background.

rationales.quote: you have just like hustled, you know, the hell out of this business
rationales.explanation: Jenny credits the founder's resourcefulness and effort in advancing the company.

rationales.quote: with multiple business models
rationales.explanation: Jenny identifies the simultaneous business-model paths as a central source of complexity behind her decision to decline.

rationales.quote: a $4 million raise, which is, you know, quite high for me as a pre-seed
rationales.explanation: Jenny explicitly says the round is large relative to her pre-seed investment parameters and links that constraint to opting out.

rationales.quote: the FDA path, I think that's going to be just a complicated one for me to get my head around
rationales.explanation: Jenny identifies the operational complexity of the FDA pathway as another reason she cannot commit.

rationales.quote: I don't think you need to decide today.
rationales.explanation: Jenny argues that the founder should not be required to revise the financing plan on the spot during the pitch.

rationales.quote: Not for us to project, though.
rationales.explanation: Jenny says the investors should not construct or project a revised plan for the founder within the pitch-room discussion.

rationales.quote: I have a business here. Oh. And I can make my business even bigger down the road when we get there.
rationales.explanation: Jenny believes the company can operate before FDA approval and use approval later to expand the business.

rationales.quote: she reversed the order and that confused us
rationales.explanation: Jenny says the founder's sequencing of the story obscured the stronger business narrative and contributed to investor confusion.

rationales.quote: Too many things.

rationales.quote: she didn't have all our numbers
rationales.explanation: Jenny agrees that the founder did not demonstrate adequate command of the financial figures during the pitch.

rationales.quote: This is pretty cool.

rationales.quote: this is the best way to accumulate the data. And I think we all just don't believe that.

rationales.quote: So you have to go through FDA, meaning that you're considered a medical device?
rationales.explanation: Jenny asks whether the product's regulatory classification requires it to be treated as a medical device.

rationales.quote: So does that mean the FDA is like a 510 or it's a, it's one of these lesser -
rationales.explanation: Jenny asks which FDA pathway the product must navigate, probing the operational burden of approval.

rationales.quote: So that's going to be shorter and less expensive.
rationales.explanation: Before being corrected, Jenny assesses the stated pathway as favorable because she believes it will require less time and capital.

rationales.quote: four million, it's a lot of money
rationales.explanation: Jenny flags the requested capital as substantial before asking how it will be deployed.

rationales.quote: what the metrics you hope to get to?
rationales.explanation: Jenny asks what measurable progress the proposed financing is expected to produce.

rationales.quote: And how's the fundraise going?
rationales.explanation: Jenny asks about current investor demand for the round.

rationales.quote: Are you looking for a lead investor? Or how are you putting the round together?
rationales.explanation: Jenny probes whether the round has or needs a lead and how its commitments are being assembled.

rationales.quote: I think that's just healthcare. That's not you.
rationales.explanation: Jenny argues that the slow sales cycle is normal for healthcare rather than evidence of founder-specific execution weakness.

rationales.quote: This is not going to change.
rationales.explanation: Jenny emphasizes that long healthcare sales cycles will remain a persistent constraint on the sales motion.

rationales.quote: I love your background
rationales.explanation: Jenny favorably assesses the founder's relevant professional background.

rationales.quote: you have just like hustled, you know, the hell out of this business
rationales.explanation: Jenny credits the founder's resourcefulness and effort in advancing the company.

rationales.quote: with multiple business models
rationales.explanation: Jenny identifies the simultaneous business-model paths as a central source of complexity behind her decision to decline.

rationales.quote: a $4 million raise, which is, you know, quite high for me as a pre-seed
rationales.explanation: Jenny explicitly says the round is large relative to her pre-seed investment parameters and links that constraint to opting out.

rationales.quote: the FDA path, I think that's going to be just a complicated one for me to get my head around
rationales.explanation: Jenny identifies the operational complexity of the FDA pathway as another reason she cannot commit.

rationales.quote: I don't think you need to decide today.
rationales.explanation: Jenny argues that the founder should not be required to revise the financing plan on the spot during the pitch.

rationales.quote: Not for us to project, though.
rationales.explanation: Jenny says the investors should not construct or project a revised plan for the founder within the pitch-room discussion.

rationales.quote: I have a business here. Oh. And I can make my business even bigger down the road when we get there.
rationales.explanation: Jenny believes the company can operate before FDA approval and use approval later to expand the business.

rationales.quote: she reversed the order and that confused us
rationales.explanation: Jenny says the founder's sequencing of the story obscured the stronger business narrative and contributed to investor confusion.

rationales.quote: Too many things.
rationales.explanation: Jenny views the number of simultaneous initiatives in the proposed plan as excessive execution scope.

rationales.quote: she didn't have all our numbers
rationales.explanation: Jenny agrees that the founder did not demonstrate adequate command of the financial figures during the pitch.

rationales.quote: This is pretty cool.
rationales.explanation: In context, Jenny favorably reacts to the company's ability to have a business even before completing FDA approval.

rationales.quote: this is the best way to accumulate the data. And I think we all just don't believe that.
rationales.explanation: Jenny rejects the founder's justification that the proposed channel strategy is the best way to gather data, explaining the investors' lack of conviction.

rationales.quote: she's not talking to enough healthcare founders
rationales.explanation: Jenny believes the founder has not done enough peer learning to calibrate expectations about healthcare sales.

rationales.quote: these deals can take six months. I'm like, that's health care, and that's not bad.
rationales.explanation: Jenny assesses a six-month healthcare sales cycle as normal rather than an adverse signal about the channel.

rationales.quote: toughen up there lady that's health care
rationales.explanation: Jenny criticizes the founder's response to ordinary healthcare sales friction and signals that greater operational persistence is needed.

rationales.quote: it can take a very long time
rationales.explanation: Jenny reiterates that lengthy sales cycles are an inherent feature of the healthcare market.
